claims.text: The GPS trace for this trip is clean: 229 fixes at a steady 10 second interval, 100% coverage, no gaps and a maximum gap of 0 seconds, so the trace is NOT impaired under POL-RD-07(a) to (c). The deviation finding therefore does not need independent corroboration under POL-RD-07(ii), and no escalation is available under POL-RD-10(3).

A route deviation is ESTABLISHED on this trip's own evidence. The trace measures 28.18 km against a booked optimal of 22.4 km, an excess of 5.78 km, which is 25.80% of optimal. Both POL-RD-01 tests pass: the excess is greater than 0.8 km in absolute terms and greater than 20% of optimal_distance_km. The governing distance field is gps_trace.trace_distance_km (28.18), not the rounded trip_record copy (28.2). The deviation is not MATERIAL (25.80% is below 50% and 5.78 km is below 8.0 km), so the POL-RD-06 materiality check is not triggered.

I do not put the rider's distance claim forward as a money claim, and I say so plainly: this trip was booked at UPFRONT_QUOTE (quoted_fare_sgd 34.50), so under POL-RD-11 the distance and time charges were fixed at booking, POL-RD-02 does not run and no distance-or-time refund is available however large the excess. The driver's 5.78 km detour cost the rider nothing on those lines and the unrecovered cost on an unjustified detour is not recoverable by the driver from the rider either. The rider's remedy lies in the overcharge on the charged total, not in the excess distance.

The rider was charged SGD 39.00 against an upfront quote of SGD 34.50 with no refund issued (payment_status CHARGED, refund_issued_sgd 0.0). Under POL-RD-11(a) the amount refundable in full is charged_total less quoted_fare_sgd plus the pass-through and statutory lines properly chargeable under POL-RD-09, namely ERP and tolls actually crossed (KPE Defu Flyover, SGD 2.50), fare_breakdown.waiting_time_fee (SGD 0.00) and any properly chargeable airport surcharge (none - this trip neither originates nor ends at an airport). That is 39.00 - (34.50 + 2.50) = SGD 2.00. The rider's full over-quote position of SGD 4.50 is reduced only by the SGD 2.50 gantry the vehicle genuinely crossed.

The AYE (Alexandra Rd towards Tuas) line of SGD 2.00 is a PHANTOM gantry charge and a billing-integrity failure under POL-RD-09(4). The trace's closest approach to that gantry's coordinates is 5,419.29 m at fix index 0, and it never comes within the 250 m match radius at any point - the note on the trace says the vehicle came no closer than 5.4 km. A charge line for a gantry the trace never passes is refunded in full as a standalone correction, available whether or not a deviation exists, and is recorded as a billing-integrity finding. Because this line is refunded under POL-RD-09(4), POL-RD-10(8) is NOT triggered by it and does not escalate the case.

For completeness and to avoid over-claiming: the KPE (Defu Flyover towards ECP) line of SGD 2.50 is NOT refundable. The trace passes that gantry within 44.50 m, well inside the 250 m match radius, and the gantry lies on the optimal route the routing engine computed for this booking. It is therefore an ERP charge actually crossed and properly chargeable, and the rider does not contest it.

The driver cannot escape this by treating the rider's two-letter reply as consent. Under POL-RD-04 the exonerating instruction must come from the RIDER and must identify a place or road specifically enough to act on; here the message 'CTE very heavy boss, i go KPE then TPE' was sent by the DRIVER at 21:14:10, and the rider's only message is 'ok' at 21:14:50, which names no place and no road. waypoint_hint is null on both messages, so the POL-RD-04 corroboration test is undecidable on the record and the clause is unavailable to the driver. It follows that POL-RD-09(3) does not bar the ERP pass-through correction: the detour was not rider-caused under POL-RD-04, POL-RD-05 or POL-RD-12.

The driver's explanation, that 'CTE northbound was heavy', is a bare assertion that carries no weight under POL-RD-08: it cites no traffic_advisory ID. There is in fact no advisory on file at all - EV-ADVIS-00115-01 is a MISSING artifact, payload null, weight_multiplier 0.0, issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT - and POL-RD-03 requires an advisory that names a road the optimal route traverses, carries a validity window overlapping the passage time, and is matched by a route leaving and rejoining the optimal corridor. No advisory exists to run that test on, so nothing is exonerated and the excess stands as established.

NO_ACTION must be read party-relative here under POL-GEN-03: this dispute was filed by the RIDER, payment_status is CHARGED and refund_issued_sgd is 0.0, so a NO_ACTION outcome would leave the whole SGD 39.00 charge standing against the rider, including the SGD 2.00 charge the trace disproves. The state that 'stands' is the state the rider is complaining about, so the rider is only made whole by a refund of the SGD 2.00 over-quote and phantom-gantry amount identified above.

claims.text: This was an UPFRONT_QUOTE trip. The fare breakdown records fare_model = UPFRONT_QUOTE with a quoted_fare_sgd of 34.50 fixed at booking, so the distance and time lines were closed at that moment. Under POL-RD-11 the platform does not recompute them: POL-RD-02 does not run and 'no distance-or-time refund is available to the rider however large the excess'. The rider's demand to refund 'the extra distance' therefore fails on the fare model itself, quite apart from the mileage, and the driver's unrecovered cost on the detour is expressly not recoverable from the rider under this clause.

The SGD 2.50 KPE (Defu Flyover towards ECP) line is a legitimate pass-through and is not refundable. It is marked on_optimal_route = true, and the 10-second trace passes within 44.5 m of that gantry (fix 136), well inside the 250 m match radius POL-RD-09 lays down for treating a fix as a crossing. ERP actually crossed on the optimal route is properly chargeable and is not returned to the rider.

The rider's entitlement under POL-RD-11 is capped at the amount by which the charged total of SGD 39.00 exceeds the SGD 34.50 quote plus the pass-through lines properly chargeable under POL-RD-09. The only properly chargeable pass-through is the SGD 2.50 KPE gantry, so the ceiling is SGD 39.00 less (SGD 34.50 + SGD 2.50) = SGD 2.00. The remaining SGD 4.00 of the SGD 6.00 contested has no basis in the record and the present state as to it should stand.

I concede the one point that is genuinely on the rider's side. The SGD 2.00 AYE (Alexandra Rd towards Tuas) line is not matched by the trace: the closest the vehicle ever comes to that gantry is 5,419 m, far outside the 250 m match radius. That is a billing-integrity failure under POL-RD-09(4) and is refunded in full as a standalone correction, available whether or not a deviation exists. The driver does not oppose that SGD 2.00; he never went near the AYE and says so; and it is not a finding against him. It is also the whole of the rider's entitlement.

The trace does show an excess — 5.78 km, 25.8% against the 22.4 km optimal, measured on the GPS polyline that POL-RD-01 makes the governing figure — so a deviation is established. It is not, however, MATERIAL: 25.8% is below the 50% limb and 5.78 km is below the 8.0 km limb. POL-RD-06 is therefore not engaged, the driver_profile check does not run, and no driver-conduct referral follows from this trip.

The driver's own explanation — heavy CTE traffic — is not carried by the record and I do not press it. The LTA advisory artifact for the 21:06-21:48 window is MISSING under issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT at weight 0.0, so no traffic_advisory names the CTE or any corridor the optimal route uses, and POL-RD-03 exoneration fails for want of the required artifact. POL-RD-08 is equally clear that a bare assertion of bad traffic, unsupported by an advisory ID, discharges nothing. The point is moot for the money, because POL-RD-11 caps the rider's recovery at SGD 2.00 in any event.

ruling.explanation:
Ruling: PARTIAL_REFUND of SGD 2.00 to the rider (the filing party). The SGD 6.00 contested reduces to the SGD 2.00 that the record actually disproves.

What the record shows. You were quoted SGD 34.50 for this trip (EV-FARE-00115). The fare breakdown shows SGD 39.00 charged, being the SGD 34.50 quote plus SGD 4.50 of ERP. The GPS trace (EV-GPS-00115: 229 fixes at 10-second intervals, 100% coverage, no gaps) measures the drive at 28.18 km against the booked optimal of 22.4 km (EV-TRIP-00115), an excess of 5.78 km or 25.8%.

Distance. A route deviation is established on this trip's own evidence — both POL-RD-01 tests pass — but it is not MATERIAL (25.8% is under the 50% limb and 5.78 km is under the 8.0 km limb), so POL-RD-06 and its driver_profile check are not engaged and no driver-conduct referral follows. Critically, this was an UPFRONT_QUOTE trip, so under POL-RD-11 the distance and time charges were fixed at booking and POL-RD-02 does not run: no distance refund is available to the rider however large the excess, and equally the driver's unrecovered detour cost is not recoverable from the rider under that clause. I have therefore not refunded the excess distance.

The money. Of the SGD 4.50 of ERP, only the SGD 2.50 KPE (Defu Flyover towards ECP) line is properly chargeable: the trace passes within 44.5 m of that gantry, inside the 250 m match radius, and it lies on the optimal route. The SGD 2.00 AYE (Alexandra Rd towards Tuas) line is a phantom — the closest the trace ever comes is 5,419 m — so the vehicle never crossed that gantry. Under POL-RD-09(4) that is a billing-integrity failure, refunded in full as a standalone correction and recorded as a referral below; POL-RD-10(8) is not triggered by it. The rider's POL-RD-11(a) ceiling is charged_total less quoted fare less the pass-throughs properly chargeable under POL-RD-09: SGD 39.00 − (SGD 34.50 + SGD 2.50 + SGD 0.00 waiting fee + SGD 0.00 airport surcharge) = SGD 2.00. The POL-RD-11(a) figure and the POL-RD-09(4) correction are the same SGD 2.00 and are not added together (POL-RD-09(1) forbids double counting). No distance was left unbilled, so no POL-RD-04 driver compensation arises.

Exculpatory points raised. The driver's explanation that CTE traffic was heavy is a bare assertion. There is no LTA advisory on file for the 21:06–21:48 window: EV-ADVIS-00115-01 is MISSING, weight 0.0, issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT, and a missing artifact carries no fact (POL-GEN-02). Under POL-RD-08 a general assertion of bad traffic unsupported by a traffic_advisory ID carries no weight and does not discharge the driver's burden, so POL-RD-03 exonerates nothing. That is a finding on the burden, not a data failure, and it does not escalate the case under POL-RD-10(5). The driver's in-app message announcing the KPE/TPE route is not a rider instruction, waypoint_hint is null on both messages, and the rider's 'ok' named no road or place, so POL-RD-04 is unavailable to either side and POL-RD-09(3) does not bar the ERP correction.

Integrity and escalation. The trace is not impaired under POL-RD-07(a)–(c): no gap over 90 s, no jump over 500 m, no sampling interval over 30 s. No independent corroboration is therefore required and POL-RD-10(3) does not apply. Trip identifiers match across the trip record, trace and fare breakdown, their timestamps agree, and the only charge line with no counterpart in the trace — the AYE line — is refunded under POL-RD-09(4), which POL-RD-10(8) expressly excludes.

Confidence. The deciding facts — the 28.18 km trace distance, the 44.5 m KPE match and the 5,419 m AYE non-match — rest on the GPS trace and the fare breakdown, each at weight 1.0, so the cap is 1.0 and confidence stands at 0.95, above the 0.70 floor.

To the rider: SGD 2.00 of your SGD 6.00 is refunded; the extra-distance element of your claim is not available on an upfront-quoted fare. To the driver: the SGD 2.50 KPE gantry stands as properly chargeable; the SGD 2.00 AYE line is refunded as a billing error, not as a finding against you.
referrals: POL-RD-09(4) billing integrity: the SGD 2.00 AYE (Alexandra Rd towards Tuas) gantry line was charged although the GPS trace never came within 250 m of that gantry (nearest fix 5,419 m at 21:10:00). Refund it in full as a standalone pass-through correction and record this billing-integrity finding.

ruling.explanation:
This was an upfront-quoted trip: the fare breakdown (EV-FARE-00115) records fare_model = UPFRONT_QUOTE with quoted_fare_sgd = 34.50. Under POL-RD-11 the distance and time charges were fixed at booking, so POL-RD-02 does not run and no distance-or-time refund is available however large the excess. The GPS trace does establish a route deviation — 28.18 km driven against a 22.4 km optimal, an excess of 5.78 km (25.8%) — but on an upfront fare that deviation costs the rider nothing on the distance lines, so the request to 'refund the extra distance' fails on the fare model itself. The deviation is established but not MATERIAL (25.8% is below the 50% limb and 5.78 km is below the 8.0 km limb), so the POL-RD-06 driver-profile check is not engaged; in any event the driver's trailing figures (deviation_flags_90d = 1 against completed_trips_90d = 174, far below the 0.05 ratio) show no pattern, and no driver-conduct referral follows.

The refund is the overcharge on the total. You were charged SGD 39.00 against the SGD 34.50 quote, and the SGD 4.50 difference is entirely ERP. The KPE (Defu Flyover towards ECP) line of SGD 2.50 is properly chargeable: the trace passes within 44.5 m of that gantry and it lies on the optimal route, so it is not returned. The AYE (Alexandra Rd towards Tuas) line of SGD 2.00 is different: the trace never comes closer than 5,419 m, so the vehicle never crossed that gantry. That is a billing-integrity failure under POL-RD-09(4), refunded in full as a standalone correction available whether or not a deviation exists, and recorded in the referrals above. Because it is the only unmatched charge line and it is refunded under POL-RD-09(4), POL-RD-10(8) does not escalate the case.

Arithmetic: charged_total 39.00 less (quoted_fare 34.50 + ERP actually crossed 2.50) = SGD 2.00, refunded in full under POL-RD-11(a). That SGD 2.00 is also exactly the phantom AYE line, so nothing is counted twice.

On the driver's attempted exoneration: POL-RD-04 is unavailable. The only message naming a route ('CTE very heavy boss, i go KPE then TPE') was sent by the driver, not the rider, and the rider's reply 'ok' names no place or road; with waypoint_hint null on both messages the corroboration test cannot be run, so the clause is unavailable and POL-RD-09(3) does not bar the ERP correction. The driver's heavy-traffic explanation is not carried by any artifact: the LTA advisory for the window is missing — EV-ADVIS-00115-01, weight 0.0, issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT — so POL-RD-03 has no advisory to run on, and a bare assertion of bad traffic discharges nothing under POL-RD-08.

The trace itself is clean under POL-RD-07 (229 fixes at a steady 10 s interval, 100% coverage, no gaps, max gap 0 s), so it is not impaired for policy purposes and needs no independent corroboration or POL-RD-10(3) escalation; its schema-level status is COMPLETE and it is used at full weight.

On the profiles: no profile field is used as a ground of decision. Only deviation_flags_90d and completed_trips_90d are citable under POL-RD-06 and they show no pattern; the remaining fields (including prior_deviation_flags, rating, account_age_days, lifetime_trips) are context only under POL-GEN-01 and were not relied on.

Reading NO_ACTION party-relatively is correct, but no NO_ACTION is reached here: this is a rider-filed dispute with payment_status CHARGED and refund_issued_sgd 0.0, so the SGD 2.00 is a real refund to the rider. Confidence rests on facts carried by EV-FARE-00115 and EV-GPS-00115, both at full weight 1.0; neither is impaired, so the cap is 1.0.
referrals: POL-RD-09(4) billing integrity: the SGD 2.00 AYE (Alexandra Rd towards Tuas) gantry line on the fare breakdown (EV-FARE-00115) was never crossed by the vehicle — the closest GPS fix is 5,419 m away, far outside the 250 m match radius — and is refunded in full as a standalone correction.

ruling.explanation: To both parties. Distance. This booking was an UPFRONT_QUOTE at SGD 34.50, so POL-RD-11 governs and POL-RD-02 does not run. The GPS trace does show a real route deviation: 28.18 km driven against the 22.4 km booking optimal, an excess of 5.78 km (25.80%), which passes both POL-RD-01 establishment tests. It is not, however, a MATERIAL deviation (25.80% is below 50% and 5.78 km is below 8.0 km), so the POL-RD-06 driver-profile check does not run and no driver-conduct referral follows. Under POL-RD-11 the distance and time lines were fixed at booking, so no part of the excess distance is refundable to the rider however large it is, and the driver cannot recover it from the rider either. That part of the claim is not payable. The charge. charged_total was SGD 39.00 against the SGD 34.50 quote, a gap of SGD 4.50, made up of two ERP lines: KPE (Defu Flyover towards ECP) SGD 2.50 and AYE (Alexandra Rd towards Tuas) SGD 2.00. The KPE gantry lies on the optimal route and the trace passes within 44.5 m of it, so it was genuinely crossed and is properly chargeable. The AYE line is different: the trace never comes closer than 5,419 m to that gantry, far outside the 250 m match radius POL-RD-09 lays down; driver, you say you never went near the AYE, and the telemetry agrees. That SGD 2.00 is a phantom charge. So SGD 39.00 less (the SGD 34.50 quote plus the SGD 2.50 gantry actually crossed) = SGD 2.00, refunded in full under POL-RD-11(a) and refunded separately and in full as a standalone correction under POL-RD-09(4); these are the same SGD 2.00 and are not counted twice. The refund is SGD 2.00 of the SGD 6.00 contested. Traffic. Driver, your explanation that the CTE was heavy cites no LTA advisory ID and no evidence ID; under POL-RD-08 that bare assertion carries no weight and discharges nothing, and POL-RD-03 exoneration cannot run without an advisory. There is no advisory on file: EV-ADVIS-00115-01 is MISSING (weight 0.0, issue MISSING_ARTIFACT), which is why nothing is exonerated on that ground; the absence itself is not held against you. Rider, I accept your reading that the two-message chat ('CTE very heavy boss, i go KPE then TPE' from the driver, 'ok' from you) does not amount to a rider instruction under POL-RD-04, so POL-RD-09(3) does not bar the ERP correction; that point is moot for the money in any event. No escalation. The trace is unimpaired under POL-RD-07 (229 fixes, steady 10-second interval, no gaps, 100% coverage); the trip identifiers match across trip record, trace and fare breakdown; and the only charge line with no counterpart in the trace is the AYE line, which is refunded under POL-RD-09(4) and so does not engage POL-RD-10(8). The driver's heavy-traffic remark is a bare assertion under POL-RD-08 rather than an exculpatory clause invoked against a cited artifact, so POL-RD-10(5) does not fire. No POL-RD-10 trigger applies and no escalation issues. Referral. The unmatched AYE line is recorded as a POL-RD-09(4) billing-integrity finding for platform review. Confidence. Every deciding figure (quote, charged total, gantry lines, deviation) is carried by full-weight artifacts — EV-FARE-00115, EV-GPS-00115 and EV-TRIP-00115, all at weight 1.0 — so confidence is high.
referrals: POL-RD-09(4) billing-integrity finding: the SGD 2.00 'AYE (Alexandra Rd towards Tuas)' ERP line is billed on a trip whose GPS trace never comes within 250 m of that gantry (closest approach 5,419.29 m, at fix index 0); the line is refunded in full as a standalone pass-through correction and is referred for billing-integrity review.

ledger.claim: The GPS trace for this trip is clean: 229 fixes at a steady 10 second interval, 100% coverage, no gaps and a maximum gap of 0 seconds, so the trace is NOT impaired under POL-RD-07(a) to (c). The deviation finding therefore does not need independent corroboration under POL-RD-07(ii), and no escalation is available under POL-RD-10(3).

A route deviation is ESTABLISHED on this trip's own evidence. The trace measures 28.18 km against a booked optimal of 22.4 km, an excess of 5.78 km, which is 25.80% of optimal. Both POL-RD-01 tests pass: the excess is greater than 0.8 km in absolute terms and greater than 20% of optimal_distance_km. The governing distance field is gps_trace.trace_distance_km (28.18), not the rounded trip_record copy (28.2). The deviation is not MATERIAL (25.80% is below 50% and 5.78 km is below 8.0 km), so the POL-RD-06 materiality check is not triggered.

I do not put the rider's distance claim forward as a money claim, and I say so plainly: this trip was booked at UPFRONT_QUOTE (quoted_fare_sgd 34.50), so under POL-RD-11 the distance and time charges were fixed at booking, POL-RD-02 does not run and no distance-or-time refund is available however large the excess. The driver's 5.78 km detour cost the rider nothing on those lines and the unrecovered cost on an unjustified detour is not recoverable by the driver from the rider either. The rider's remedy lies in the overcharge on the charged total, not in the excess distance.

The rider was charged SGD 39.00 against an upfront quote of SGD 34.50 with no refund issued (payment_status CHARGED, refund_issued_sgd 0.0). Under POL-RD-11(a) the amount refundable in full is charged_total less quoted_fare_sgd plus the pass-through and statutory lines properly chargeable under POL-RD-09, namely ERP and tolls actually crossed (KPE Defu Flyover, SGD 2.50), fare_breakdown.waiting_time_fee (SGD 0.00) and any properly chargeable airport surcharge (none - this trip neither originates nor ends at an airport). That is 39.00 - (34.50 + 2.50) = SGD 2.00. The rider's full over-quote position of SGD 4.50 is reduced only by the SGD 2.50 gantry the vehicle genuinely crossed.

The AYE (Alexandra Rd towards Tuas) line of SGD 2.00 is a PHANTOM gantry charge and a billing-integrity failure under POL-RD-09(4). The trace's closest approach to that gantry's coordinates is 5,419.29 m at fix index 0, and it never comes within the 250 m match radius at any point - the note on the trace says the vehicle came no closer than 5.4 km. A charge line for a gantry the trace never passes is refunded in full as a standalone correction, available whether or not a deviation exists, and is recorded as a billing-integrity finding. Because this line is refunded under POL-RD-09(4), POL-RD-10(8) is NOT triggered by it and does not escalate the case.

For completeness and to avoid over-claiming: the KPE (Defu Flyover towards ECP) line of SGD 2.50 is NOT refundable. The trace passes that gantry within 44.50 m, well inside the 250 m match radius, and the gantry lies on the optimal route the routing engine computed for this booking. It is therefore an ERP charge actually crossed and properly chargeable, and the rider does not contest it.

The driver cannot escape this by treating the rider's two-letter reply as consent. Under POL-RD-04 the exonerating instruction must come from the RIDER and must identify a place or road specifically enough to act on; here the message 'CTE very heavy boss, i go KPE then TPE' was sent by the DRIVER at 21:14:10, and the rider's only message is 'ok' at 21:14:50, which names no place and no road. waypoint_hint is null on both messages, so the POL-RD-04 corroboration test is undecidable on the record and the clause is unavailable to the driver. It follows that POL-RD-09(3) does not bar the ERP pass-through correction: the detour was not rider-caused under POL-RD-04, POL-RD-05 or POL-RD-12.

The driver's explanation, that 'CTE northbound was heavy', is a bare assertion that carries no weight under POL-RD-08: it cites no traffic_advisory ID. There is in fact no advisory on file at all - EV-ADVIS-00115-01 is a MISSING artifact, payload null, weight_multiplier 0.0, issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT - and POL-RD-03 requires an advisory that names a road the optimal route traverses, carries a validity window overlapping the passage time, and is matched by a route leaving and rejoining the optimal corridor. No advisory exists to run that test on, so nothing is exonerated and the excess stands as established.

NO_ACTION must be read party-relative here under POL-GEN-03: this dispute was filed by the RIDER, payment_status is CHARGED and refund_issued_sgd is 0.0, so a NO_ACTION outcome would leave the whole SGD 39.00 charge standing against the rider, including the SGD 2.00 charge the trace disproves. The state that 'stands' is the state the rider is complaining about, so the rider is only made whole by a refund of the SGD 2.00 over-quote and phantom-gantry amount identified above.

This was an UPFRONT_QUOTE trip. The fare breakdown records fare_model = UPFRONT_QUOTE with a quoted_fare_sgd of 34.50 fixed at booking, so the distance and time lines were closed at that moment. Under POL-RD-11 the platform does not recompute them: POL-RD-02 does not run and 'no distance-or-time refund is available to the rider however large the excess'. The rider's demand to refund 'the extra distance' therefore fails on the fare model itself, quite apart from the mileage, and the driver's unrecovered cost on the detour is expressly not recoverable from the rider under this clause.

The SGD 2.50 KPE (Defu Flyover towards ECP) line is a legitimate pass-through and is not refundable. It is marked on_optimal_route = true, and the 10-second trace passes within 44.5 m of that gantry (fix 136), well inside the 250 m match radius POL-RD-09 lays down for treating a fix as a crossing. ERP actually crossed on the optimal route is properly chargeable and is not returned to the rider.

The rider's entitlement under POL-RD-11 is capped at the amount by which the charged total of SGD 39.00 exceeds the SGD 34.50 quote plus the pass-through lines properly chargeable under POL-RD-09. The only properly chargeable pass-through is the SGD 2.50 KPE gantry, so the ceiling is SGD 39.00 less (SGD 34.50 + SGD 2.50) = SGD 2.00. The remaining SGD 4.00 of the SGD 6.00 contested has no basis in the record and the present state as to it should stand.

I concede the one point that is genuinely on the rider's side. The SGD 2.00 AYE (Alexandra Rd towards Tuas) line is not matched by the trace: the closest the vehicle ever comes to that gantry is 5,419 m, far outside the 250 m match radius. That is a billing-integrity failure under POL-RD-09(4) and is refunded in full as a standalone correction, available whether or not a deviation exists. The driver does not oppose that SGD 2.00; he never went near the AYE and says so; and it is not a finding against him. It is also the whole of the rider's entitlement.

The trace does show an excess — 5.78 km, 25.8% against the 22.4 km optimal, measured on the GPS polyline that POL-RD-01 makes the governing figure — so a deviation is established. It is not, however, MATERIAL: 25.8% is below the 50% limb and 5.78 km is below the 8.0 km limb. POL-RD-06 is therefore not engaged, the driver_profile check does not run, and no driver-conduct referral follows from this trip.

The driver's own explanation — heavy CTE traffic — is not carried by the record and I do not press it. The LTA advisory artifact for the 21:06-21:48 window is MISSING under issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT at weight 0.0, so no traffic_advisory names the CTE or any corridor the optimal route uses, and POL-RD-03 exoneration fails for want of the required artifact. POL-RD-08 is equally clear that a bare assertion of bad traffic, unsupported by an advisory ID, discharges nothing. The point is moot for the money, because POL-RD-11 caps the rider's recovery at SGD 2.00 in any event.
